content: 1. The combination of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled with drugs that prolong the QTc interval can increase toxicity. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Extreme caution is advised when vilanterol is coadministered with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be amplified. 2. Pentamidine and vandetanib both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs is necessary, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 3. Vemurafenib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. 4. Pentamidine and venlafaxine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Pentamidine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 6. Pentamidine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Vorinostat and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Albuterol and pentamidine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 9. Pentamidine and alfuzosin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 10. Amikacin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 11. Amphotericin B deoxycholate and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of atogepant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of avapritinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Pentamidine increases levels of axitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Azithromycin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Pentamidine and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 17. Pentamidine and canagliflozin both increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 18. Cannabidiol increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when coadministered with cannabidiol. 19. Carboplatin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 20. Cenobamate increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider a dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. 21. Cidofovir and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Ciprofloxacin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but caution is advised when combined with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 23. Cisplatin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 24. Pentamidine and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. ECG monitoring is recommended. 25. Iodinated contrast media and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 26. Crizotinib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. ECG monitoring is recommended. 27. Cyclosporine and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 28. Deutetrabenazine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 29. Elagolix increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor; caution is advised with sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 30. Pentamidine and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 31. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Etravirine increases levels of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. There is potential for increased toxicity. 33. Ezogabine and pentamidine both increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at high doses. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 34. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of CYP2C19 substrates as necessary. 35. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of finerenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 37. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if coadministered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Pentamidine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 39. Gadobenate and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 40. Pentamidine and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 41. Gepirone and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Glucarpidase decreases the level or effect of pentamidine by increasing metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Glucarpidase hydrolyzes glutamate residues from folic acid and antifolates. 43. Goserelin increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 44. Histrelin increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 45. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 46. Ifosfamide and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. Renal function should be monitored. 47. Indacaterol inhaled and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 48. Pentamidine and insulin aspart may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 49. Pentamidine and insulin aspart protamine/insulin aspart may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 50. Pentamidine and insulin degludec may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 51. Pentamidine and insulin degludec/insulin aspart may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pentamidine may either increase or decrease the blood glucose-lowering effect of antidiabetic agents. It may cause hypoglycemia, which may sometimes be followed by hyperglycemia. 52. Pentamidine and insulin detemir may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 53. Pentamidine and insulin glargine may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 54. Pentamidine and insulin glulisine may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 55. Pentamidine and inhaled insulin may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 56. Pentamidine and insulin isophane human/insulin regular human may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 57. Pentamidine and insulin lispro may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 58. Pentamidine and insulin lispro protamine/insulin lispro may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 59. Pentamidine and insulin NPH may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 60. Pentamidine and insulin regular human may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Pentamidine may cause hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, sometimes followed by the opposite effect. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required. 61. Ioversol and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 62. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Pentamidine increases levels of ivacaftor by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of lemborexant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended if coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 65. Pentamidine and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 66. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 67. Pentamidine increases levels of lomitapide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lomitapide dosage should not exceed 30 mg/day. 68. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor and pentamidine interact by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. In vitro studies suggest lumacaftor may induce and ivacaftor may inhibit CYP2C19 substrates. 69. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of mavacamten by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 70. Mavorixafor and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Mavorixafor dose reduction or discontinuation may be required. 71. Pentamidine decreases the effects of metformin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 72. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of intranasal midazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 73. Mifepristone and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 74. Neomycin PO and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 75. Pentamidine and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the effects of beta-2 agonists on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 76. Osilodrostat and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 77. Osimertinib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 78. Oxaliplatin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 79. Ozanimod and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
